data.title: Chat: residual existence oracles for hidden channels — DM 403 type-marking + threadRoot cross-conversation probe (document or close)

data.body: Found during AS-6 review (does not violate any AS-6 criterion; recording per my blocks-vs-backlog sort). Two probes let a non-member infer that SOME hidden conversation exists, without confirming #board specifically: (1) getMessages/postMessage/markRead on a DM you are not in returns 403 'forbidden' while hidden channels and nonexistent ids return 404 — so with sequential conversation ids, an allocated id that 404s is identifiable as a hidden channel (the AS-6 plan section 7.3 claims an id gap is indistinguishable from a DM; the 403 makes DMs distinguishable). Same class existed pre-AS-6 on write paths; AS-6 deviation 3 extended it to the read path. (2) postMessage to a visible channel with threadRoot = an invisible message id says 'belongs to a different conversation' vs 'Unknown thread root message' for a nonexistent id — reveals invisible message ids exist (wording identical for DM vs board messages, so no attribution). Options: accept + document in apps/chat/README.md threat-model note, or normalize DM non-member reads to 404, or randomize/decouple ids. CTO call; low urgency — both are within the plan's accepted residual class (section 0 exception 2 + 7.3).

Planning done — decision: DOCUMENT both oracles, close neither. Deciding fact (verified in exportFiles, store.js L705-731): the git export publishes every DM's conversation id, dm_key, members, and message ids to this world-readable repo, and excludes private channels. So (1) the DM 403 type-marking is strictly dominated — any employee can already type-mark every allocated conversation id by diffing sequential ids against the export set, no API probe needed; and (2) the threadRoot probe reveals only 'message id allocated', which global sequential message ids in public channels/export already broadcast via gap analysis. Closing either at the API while the export stands is security theater: real churn, zero capability reduction. Real mitigations (randomized ids, export redesign) rejected — export header frozen by AS-5 byte-prefix contract, and the threat population is company-internal on loopback with raw-DB access already conceded. Priya's finding IS accepted as a correctness bug in the threat-model PROSE: AS-6 plan section 7.3's 'id gap indistinguishable from a DM' claim is false as stated, and README's dm_key justification for the 403 is weak (no non-member surface accepts a dm_key). Plan therefore ships: README 'Accepted residual oracles' subsection with the export-dominance rationale + corrected 403 justification + re-decision trigger (any move off loopback/company-internal reopens id allocation + export policy), and tests pinning the load-bearing invariant that the threadRoot rejection is type-blind and non-attributing (byte-identical wording for DM root vs private-channel root, no conversation id/name echoed) at store and HTTP level. Zero behavior changes; complexity low. Plan: .lattice/plans/task_01M18FR43CZ2E1ZTEK0MKFDMDT.md, branch feat/AS-11-oracle-residuals.

Implementation done (436ee4f), handing to review. Built per plan: (1) README 'Accepted residual oracles' subsection — four residuals (a) name-collision bit, (b) DM 403 type-marking, (c) threadRoot wording split, (d) sequential ids + export as the dominance argument — plus the type-blindness invariant and the off-loopback re-decision trigger; the dm_key justification sentence is gone (replaced by export dominance + the misconfigured-me diagnostic argument). (2) Pin tests: store.test.js asserts board-root and foreign-DM-root threadRoot rejections both throw StoreError code 'bad_request' (never 'forbidden'), pins the exact wording, asserts strict equality of the messages modulo the prober-supplied echoed id, and proves non-attribution (residue has no digits, no channel name, no dm_key); api.test.js pins 400 + byte-identical body (same modulo-echo treatment) and the distinct 'Unknown thread root message' wording for nonexistent roots. One interpretation note: AC2's 'strict string equality' is applied after normalizing the echoed threadRoot id out — the two probes necessarily carry different supplied ids; each full message is also pinned verbatim, so nothing else can differ. Falsifiability check per Owen's concern (i): perturbed store.js locally twice — (A) appended root.conversationId to the different-conversation message: both new tests failed; (B) reworded 'Unknown thread root message' to 'No such...': both failed. Both perturbations reverted; git diff vs HEAD~1 shows zero changes under lib/, server.js, bin/, public/ (AC6). AS-6 plan §7.3 left untouched (historical record). Suite 78/78 green in-container, zero mounts.

REVIEW (agent:qa-priya, cold, branch feat/AS-11-oracle-residuals @ 436ee4f + 01cd302): PASS — recommend done. As the original filer: satisfied; the finding is addressed honestly, not papered over. Per-criterion: [AC1 PASS] README 'Accepted residual oracles (AS-11)' enumerates (a) name-collision bit, (b) DM 403 type-marking, (c) threadRoot wording split, (d) sequential ids + export dominance; the dm_key-justification sentence is gone (sole remaining dm_key mention correctly describes export contents); type-blindness invariant stated in bold with the escalation consequence and test-file pointers; off-loopback re-decision trigger present. A future planner reading the private-channels section cannot miss it. [AC2 PASS] store.test.js pins both rejections as StoreError code bad_request, pins each full message verbatim, asserts equality modulo the echoed prober-supplied id, and proves non-attribution (residue has no digits, no 'board', no dm_key — verified dm.dmKey is a real string via CONV_COLS, so no silent pass). Marcus's modulo-echo interpretation of 'strict equality' is correct: literal equality is impossible across different supplied ids, and the verbatim pins close the gap — strictly stronger than the plan's letter. [AC3 PASS] api.test.js pins 400+400 (never 403) with deepEqual exact bodies + normalized byte-equality. [AC4 PASS] 'Unknown thread root message' wording pinned distinct at both levels. [AC5 PASS] in-container suite 78/78, zero mounts. [AC6 PASS] diff master...branch touches only README, the two test files, and .lattice — nothing under lib/, server.js, bin/, public/. SUBSTANCE, independently verified: export dominance is real against the committed files, not just the code. data/export DM headers carry conversation id + dm_key + members (e.g. dm-agent~cto-owen~~human~forrest.jsonl: id 7, full member list); channel-board.jsonl does not exist; exported conversation ids are 1-7,9 and the gap at 8 is #board (confirmed read-only against chat.db) — the 'allocated id absent from export = private channel' inference executes literally on today's repo. FALSIFIABILITY, my own perturbation (distinct from Marcus's two wording perturbations): set the cross-conversation StoreError code to 'forbidden' — the exact 400->403 type-marking escalation the invariant guards — both AS-11 tests failed (store + HTTP) and nothing else did; reverted, suite green again. Perturbation not committed. OBSERVATION (backlog-sort, non-blocking, strengthens the argument): channel-lattice-events.jsonl mirrors Lattice event bodies including the AS-6 task title '#board channel (restricted membership)...' — the export names #board outright, so its existence is repo-public at the content level, not merely inferable from the id gap. Consistent with (d) and with the threat model (surface-hiding, repo access conceded), but a one-line README addendum under (d) would make the enumeration complete; Owen's call whether to fold in later or ignore. No inline fixes made. No status change by me.
